beats.narration_en: Why don't police spike strips make tires explode?
Because a blowout at sixty could flip the car right over.
So every spike is a hollow steel tube with a sharp tip.
As the tire rolls across, the tubes punch into the tread.
Then they snap off the strip and stay stuck in the rubber.
Air leaks out through each tube, like breathing through a straw.
The tire goes flat in about half a minute, instead of bursting.
So the car slows down on its own, still steering straight.
That's how a chase ends without a crash.
